lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I heard, Chiron, that being a god, you actually wanted to die.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: You heard right, Menippus. I'm dead, as you can see — and I could have been immortal.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: What sort of passion for death came over you? Most people don't find it especially lovable.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: I'll tell you — you're not unintelligent. There was simply no pleasure left in enjoying immortality.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No pleasure in being alive and seeing the light?

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: No, Menippus. Pleasure, the way I see it, is something varied — not uniform. And I was alive forever, enjoying the same things: sun, light, food, the same seasons, every event following the next in order, one thing always trailing after another. [pause] I'd had my fill. Pleasure doesn't lie in always having a thing — it lies just as much in going without it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well put, Chiron. And how do you find the underworld, now that you've chosen your way down here?

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: Not unpleasant, Menippus. The equality is thoroughly democratic, and frankly it makes no real difference whether you're in the light or the dark. Besides — no thirst here, no hunger, none of that business. We're past needing any of it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Careful, Chiron — make sure your argument doesn't fall over its own feet.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well — if sameness and repetition wore you out up there, then sameness down here will wear you out the same way eventually. And then you'll need another change, another life after this one. Which I suspect [pause] isn't on offer.

lines.speaker: Chiron
lines.text: So what's a person to do, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: The sensible thing, as they say: be content with what you've got, take it as it comes, and don't decide any of it is unbearable.
